test: MTP (qwen3_next_mtp / mtp) speculative decoding feasibility on 2× RTX 3090
_WARNING_config_confound: This MTP run used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.80 --max-num-seqs 2` while the no-MTP baseline (results/dialog_baseline.json) used `0.90 / 8`. The published -12% delta therefore conflates MTP-method effect with serve-config effect. The original 0.80/2 was chosen out of OOM caution that the boot_findings block below shows is unnecessary (~0.79 GB per-card overhead, well under the 0.90/0.80 gap). For a clean apples-to-apples MTP A/B with matched flags, see results/modal_2x_a100_v2.json (2x A100-80GB SXM4 NVLink, prompt-4 decode-only delta -11.4%, TTFT-robust).
boot_verdict: MTP boots successfully on 24GB Ampere with gpu_memory_utilization=0.80. Earlier reports of OOM were due to robot_brain Whisper occupying ~1.6GB on GPU0 + gpu_memory_utilization=0.90 leaving no headroom. With those resolved, MTP loads cleanly. Drafter sharing lm_head and embedding weights with target keeps overhead small.

decode_bench.harness: 5 prompts × max_tokens=200 × temperature=0.5 × seed=42 (same set used in baseline)

verdict: MTP k=1 is a NET LOSS on this configuration for diverse voice-dialog prompts. Mean throughput drops 12% with huge variance. Best-case acceptance gives +12% speedup but worst-case rejection costs -40% (all the verification overhead with no payoff). For a baseline as fast as 126 tok/s, the MTP draft must achieve very high acceptance rate to be net-positive — and qwen3.6's MTP heads on AWQ-Marlin Q4 don't clear that bar on diverse prompts.
recommendation: DO NOT enable MTP for low-latency single-stream voice dialog on RTX 3090 + AWQ-Marlin. Stick with the no-MTP baseline (126 tok/s, near-zero variance). MTP may still help in batched server scenarios where the verification cost amortizes across requests — untested here.
what_did_not_kill_it: OOM was avoidable. MTP draft is ~0.8GB extra per card, not a 2× model copy.
what_killed_it: Acceptance rate. The k=1 draft predictions disagreed with the target enough that mean throughput net-decreased.
